title: Lift a calibrated face law if a paid weighted-slice bound holds
statement: For supplied support D=n.x-b>=0 and given theta of numerical magnitude<=B, let Z_k=sum_{D=k}exp(theta.x)/x! and M_k=sum_{D=k}(1+||x||1)exp(theta.x)/x!. ASSUME a computable fixed-R polynomial P_R and the inequalities M_k<=Z_0 2^[P_R(L+B)(k+1)] for EVERY k>=1, with the face-conditioned mean already close to m. Choosing T=3P_R(L+B)+ceil(log2(16/epsilon))+10 makes sum_{k>=1}2^-Tk M_k/Z_0<epsilon/8 by a geometric series. Thus theta-Tn log2 lifts the face law with small full-law mean error, with normal/output cost polynomial in L+B and log accuracy when numerical normal size is controlled. The slice-growth assumption is NOT proved by local witnesses, conformal words, a finite-support comparator or target-centred suppression; arbitrary tangential tilts may create huge unconditioned Poisson means. This is a complete conditional implication, not a universal inverse compiler.
